title: Indian Men's Team Assured of Asian Games Medal After Victory Over Japan
indian_angle: This marks the first time in 40 years that the Indian men's team has secured back-to-back medals at the continental event, highlighting their consistent performance.
summary: The Indian men's badminton team defeated Japan in the Asian Games quarterfinals, guaranteeing themselves at least a bronze medal. This achievement continues their strong run, following a silver medal in 2023 and bronzes in 1974, 1982, and 1986.

title: Sindhu-Led Indian Women's Team Exits Asian Games After QF Loss to Japan
indian_angle: Despite a win from Treesa Jolly and Gayatri Gopichand, the Indian women's team, led by PV Sindhu, could not advance past the quarterfinals, ending their medal hopes.
summary: The Indian women's badminton team was knocked out of the Asian Games after a 1-3 loss to Japan in the quarterfinals. While the doubles pair of Treesa Jolly and Gayatri Gopichand secured a win against Yuki Fukushima and Mayu Matsumoto, the team ultimately fell short.

title: BAI Level-1 Advanced Coaches Course Held in Guwahati and Raipur
indian_angle: This course is crucial for enhancing the coaching standards across India, directly impacting the development of future Indian badminton talent.
summary: Badminton Association of India (BAI) conducted its Level-1 (Advanced) Coaches Course at the National Centers of Excellence in Guwahati and Raipur from September 14 to 23, 2026, aiming to upskill coaches nationwide.

title: Indian Junior Team Coaching Camp for Asia U17 & U15 Championships
indian_angle: The camp at NCE Guwahati is vital for preparing India's promising young shuttlers for the upcoming Badminton Asia U17 & U15 Junior Championships.
summary: A national coaching camp for the Indian team participating in the Badminton Asia U17 & U15 Junior Championships 2026 was held at the National Center of Excellence in Guwahati, focusing on preparing the young talents for international competition.

title: BAI Implements 3x15 Scoring System for Domestic Junior Tournaments
indian_angle: This new scoring system will be implemented in domestic ranking tournaments and national championships for U-13, U-15, and U-17 categories, affecting many young Indian players.
summary: The Badminton Association of India has announced the implementation of a 3x15 scoring system for all domestic ranking tournaments and national championships in the U-13, U-15, and U-17 age groups, effective from June 30, 2026.
